teaching_examples.text: Se mann cōm, and hē geseah ðæt hūs.
teaching_examples.translation: The man came, and he saw the house.
teaching_examples.context_display_obligation: Print the context immediately before this example, kept on the same page with the Old English and its translation.

teaching_examples.text: Se mann geseah ðæt hūs ðe his sunu geworhte.
teaching_examples.translation: The man saw the house which his son had built.
teaching_examples.target: Context: the house was finished before the visit. A simple preterite can represent the earlier past event.
teaching_examples.context: The house was finished before the man’s visit.
teaching_examples.context_display_obligation: Print the context immediately before this example, kept on the same page with the Old English and its translation.

teaching_examples.text: Nū hæbbe ic ðæt hūs geworht.
teaching_examples.translation: Now I have built the house.
teaching_examples.target: Present habban with a completed action and its result.
teaching_examples.context_display_obligation: Print the context immediately before this example, kept on the same page with the Old English and its translation.

teaching_examples.text: Ðā se sunu cōm, hæfde se mann ðæt hūs geworht.
teaching_examples.translation: When the son came, the man had built the house.
teaching_examples.target: Past viewpoint: the building is anterior to the arrival.
teaching_examples.context: The building was already complete when the son arrived.
teaching_examples.context_display_obligation: Print the context immediately before this example, kept on the same page with the Old English and its translation.

teaching_examples.text: Se mann band ðæt hors. Ðæt hors wearð bunden.
teaching_examples.translation: The man bound the horse. The horse was bound.
teaching_examples.target: Active and agentless passive with the affected entity as subject.
teaching_examples.context_display_obligation: Print the context immediately before this example, kept on the same page with the Old English and its translation.

teaching_examples.target: An ordinary state/result reading, without an absolute wesan/event prohibition.
teaching_examples.context: The context presents the horse in its resulting bound state; wesan does not invariably exclude an event reading.
teaching_examples.context_display_obligation: Print the context immediately before this example, kept on the same page with the Old English and its translation.

teaching_examples.target: Recognition: wesan with an intransitive past participle, not passive.
teaching_examples.context: In a past account, the man’s departure precedes the next event.
teaching_examples.context_display_obligation: Print the context immediately before this example, kept on the same page with the Old English and its translation.

teaching_examples.target: Recognition: present participle periphrasis, with interpretation supplied by context.
teaching_examples.context: The account describes a period during which the man was seated.
teaching_examples.context_display_obligation: Print the context immediately before this example, kept on the same page with the Old English and its translation.

teaching_examples.text: Hē sægð ðæt hē sīe hēr. Hē sægde ðæt hē wǣre hēr.
teaching_examples.translation: He says that he is here. He said that he was here.
teaching_examples.target: In both reports the presence is simultaneous with the saying.
teaching_examples.context: In each report, the presence is simultaneous with the saying.
teaching_examples.context_display_obligation: Print the context immediately before this example, kept on the same page with the Old English and its translation.

teaching_examples.text: Hē sægde ðæt hē ðæt hūs geworht hæfde.
teaching_examples.translation: He said that he had built the house.
teaching_examples.target: A completed action anterior to a past report.
teaching_examples.context: The building precedes the past saying.
teaching_examples.context_display_obligation: Print the context immediately before this example, kept on the same page with the Old English and its translation.

teaching_examples.text: Hē sægde ðæt hē wolde cuman.
teaching_examples.translation: He said that he intended to come.
teaching_examples.target: Intention is reported; actual arrival is not asserted.
teaching_examples.context: The speaker reports an intention; the sentence does not establish whether the arrival occurred.

teaching_examples.target: Context: the visit is still expected. Present morphology can have future reference.

new_reading.title: A house and a return
new_reading.text: Se mann hæfde ān hūs geworht. Ðā cōm his sunu, and se sunu geseah ðæt hūs. Se fæder cwæð: “Nū hæbbe ic ðæt hūs geworht.” Se sunu sægde ðæt hē wolde faran. Ðā se sunu gewāt, ðā sæt se fæder on ðǣm hūse. Ðā cōm se sunu, and hē sealde his fæder męte.
